prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

Summary of Green Party Manifesto 2024 (policy-focused, max 500 words)

Health and social care
- NHS: Additional revenue spending in England rising to £28bn by 2030; capital at least £20bn over five years. Priorities include reducing waiting lists, rapid GP access (same-day for urgent need), universal NHS dentistry access (£3bn/yr by 2030), increased staff pay, £1.5bn immediate public health restoration, £2bn primary care capital, community diagnostics, National Cancer Plan, 28‑day access to mental health therapies, counsellors in every school/college, assisted dying with safeguards, end new HIV transmissions by 2030.
- Social care: Free personal care; £20bn/yr investment; national pay/career structure for care workers; visa system reform to prevent exploitation. Children’s social care: +£3bn to councils. Disability: 5% benefit uplift; oppose PIP voucher plans; SEND transport entitlements; workplace support.

Housing and planning
- 150,000 new social homes per year; end Right to Buy; rent controls via local authorities; end Section 21 evictions; tenant right to energy upgrades.
- Retrofit and standards: £29bn over five years to insulate homes (ten‑year programme), £9bn low‑carbon heating, £7bn overheating adaptation; £4bn to insulate public buildings. New homes to Passivhaus‑equivalent with solar and low‑carbon heating; upgrade PRS to EPC C. Empty homes powers; first‑refusal purchase rights for social landlords on certain properties. Planning reforms to integrate services, protect green spaces, require whole‑life carbon assessment, prioritise reuse of materials.

Energy and climate
- No new oil/gas licences; end subsidies; carbon tax starting £120/tCO2e rising to up to £500/t within 10 years. Nuclear: stop new build; phase out existing.
- Targets: Wind ~70% of electricity by 2030; by 2035: 80GW offshore wind, 53GW onshore wind, 100GW solar. End onshore wind restrictions; expand grid, storage, and interconnectors; support green hydrogen for industry. Community ownership thresholds; Local Electricity Bill; stop imported biomass subsidies (e.g., Drax).

Economy and taxation
- Green investment averaging £40bn/yr (power, buildings, rail, public transport, active travel, industry, water/sewage, nationalisations). Bring railways, water companies and Big 5 retail energy suppliers into public ownership.
- Finance: Mandate fossil divestment by 2030 across regulated institutions; BoE mandate to support transition; credit guidance away from unsustainable activities.
- Taxes: Wealth tax (1% >£10m; 2% >£1bn); align CGT and investment income rates with earnings; remove NI upper earnings limit; reform IHT; revalue Council Tax; steps toward Land Value Tax; windfall taxes on oil/gas and banks; VAT changes (reduce for hospitality/arts; increase for private education/financial services). Carbon tax as above. Borrow to invest, with inflation-capacity constraint.

Work and welfare
- Minimum wage £15/hr (support for SMEs via Employment Allowance to £10k); workers’ rights from day one; repeal anti‑union laws; 10:1 pay ratio guidance; full rights for platform workers; expanded pay‑gap reporting; move toward shorter working week.
- Social security: +£40/week to UC and legacy benefits; scrap 5‑week wait; abolish two‑child cap; end sanctions; disability benefits +5%; protect pensions; carer’s allowance +10%; scrap bedroom tax. Long‑term goal: Universal Basic Income.

Nature, animals, food
- 30% of land and sea protected by 2030; Rights of Nature Act; Clean Air Act; increase DEFRA by £1.5bn; nationalise water; right to roam; peatland rewetting, woodland expansion, urban biodiversity measures; fully protected MPAs; ban destructive fishing.
- Animal measures: Commission on Animal Protection; ban blood sports; phase out factory farming practices; end badger cull; reduce animal testing.
- Food/farming: Nearly triple farm support toward nature‑friendly methods; cut pesticides; expand horticulture; end unfair trade deals; free school meals for all children and breakfast clubs to Year 6.

Education
- Schools: +£8bn (incl. £2bn for teacher pay); £2.5bn/yr for safe buildings; more SEND funding (£5bn); end high‑stakes testing, abolish Ofsted; free meals; counsellors and nurses in schools.
- Post‑16/FE: +£3bn for sixth forms; £12bn for skills/lifelong learning.
- HE: Scrap tuition fees; restore maintenance grants; address sector pension cost pressures.

Transport
- Public transport: Subsidies rising to £10bn/yr; £19bn over five years for PT and active travel; public ownership of rail; local control of buses; £2.5bn/yr for cycleways/footpaths.
- Roads/vehicles: Oppose new roads; restore fuel duty escalator; road pricing; end new ICE sales by 2027 and road use by 2035; £5bn/yr EV scrappage by end of parliament; weight‑based road tax; 20mph default in built‑up areas.
- Aviation: Frequent‑flyer levy; ban domestic flights where rail <3h; carbon tax on kerosene; no airport expansion.

Democracy, rights, migration
- Proportional representation; repeal voter‑ID; replace Lords with elected chamber; votes at 16; transparency and party finance reforms; protect Human Rights Act and ECHR access; repeal recent protest‑limiting laws; self‑ID for trans people.
- Migration: End “hostile environment”; safe routes; permit work for asylum seekers; simplify visas; fees at cost; end routine detention; voting rights for visa holders; NHS access; remove spousal income rules.

Justice and policing
- End routine stop‑and‑search and facial recognition; expand restorative justice; presumption against custodial sentences under two years; decriminalise drug possession with diversion to support; invest up to £11bn over parliament in courts/legal aid; national strategy to tackle violence against women and girls; decriminalise sex work; restore youth services.

Foreign policy
- Uphold international law; support Ukraine; rejoin EU (Customs Union first, free movement, Erasmus); immediate ceasefire in Israel‑Gaza, recognise Palestine, end UK arms exports to Israel; aid to 1% GNI and climate finance to 1.5% GNI by 2033; support ecocide law; debt relief; sign TPNW, cancel Trident; work within NATO with reforms including No First Use.
